title: Broccoli Cheese
subtitle: British broccoli in a cheddar bechamel sauce
excerpt: Broccoli florets baked in a thick cheddar sauce with a cheesy, bubbling top. A British classic side dish that works alongside a roast or as a weeknight main.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from British cauliflower and broccoli cheese traditions. The roux-based bechamel is the standard approach; the mustard and nutmeg are consistent across most reliable versions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead and keep in the fridge. Add 5 minutes to the baking time if going in cold.

content.text: Cook the roux for a full minute before adding the milk. This cooks out the raw flour taste.

items.prepNote: grated; 100g stirred into the sauce, 100g scattered on top

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the broccoli for 3 minutes until just tender. Drain well.
Make the sauce in the same saucepan. Melt the butter over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk a little at a time, whisking after each addition. Keep whisking until the sauce is smooth and has no lumps.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is thick and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from heat. Stir in the mustard, nutmeg, and 100g of the grated cheddar. Season well.
Put the broccoli in a baking dish or roasting tin. Pour the cheese sauce over the top. Scatter the remaining 100g of cheddar evenly over the surface.
Bake for 20 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. Serve straight from the dish.

items.cause: Milk was added too fast before whisking.
items.fix: Add milk in small splashes and whisk fully between each addition.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and gluey.
items.cause: Too much flour or not enough milk.
items.fix: Whisk in an extra 50ml of milk and heat gently until smooth.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough or not enough cheese on top.
items.fix: Flash under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes to finish.
